'''David Soudry''' (born 1956<ref name="advances"/>) is a professor of mathematics at [[Tel Aviv University]] working in [[number theory]] and [[automorphic forms]].

==Career==
Soudry was born in 1956.<ref name="advances">{{cite book |title=Advances in the Theory of Automorphic Forms and Their L-functions |editor-first1=Dihua |editor-last1=Jiang |editor-link1=Dihua Jiang |editor-first2=Freydoon |editor-last2=Shahidi |editor-link2=Freydoon Shahidi |editor-first3=David |editor-last3=Soudry |series=Contemporary Mathematics |volume=664 |page=i}}</ref> He received his PhD in mathematics from Tel Aviv University in 1983 under the supervision of [[Ilya Piatetski-Shapiro]].<ref name="mathgenealogy">{{MathGenealogy|id=147561}}</ref> From 1983 to 1984, he was a member of the [[Institute for Advanced Study]].<ref name="IAS">{{cite web |url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/david-soudry |title=David Soudry |date=9 December 2019 |publisher=[[Institute for Advanced Study]] |access-date=29 February 2020}}</ref> He is a professor of mathematics at Tel Aviv University.<ref name="Homepage">{{cite web|url=https://english.tau.ac.il/profile/soudry |publisher=[[Tel Aviv University]] |title=Prof. David Soudry |access-date=29 February 2020}}</ref>

==Research==
Together with [[Stephen Rallis]] and [[David Ginzburg]], Soudry wrote a series of papers about automorphic descent culminating in their book ''The descent map from automorphic representations of GL(''n'') to classical groups.'' Their automorphic descent method constructs an explicit inverse map to the (standard) [[Langlands program#Functoriality|Langlands functorial lift]] and has had major applications to the analysis of functoriality.<ref>J. Cogdell, H. Jacquet, D. Jiang, S. Kudla, (2015), eds. "Steve Rallis (1942–2012)," ''Journal of Number Theory'', 146, 1–3</ref>  Also, using the "Rallis tower property" from Rallis's 1984 paper on the [[Howe duality conjecture]], they studied global exceptional correspondences and found new examples of functorial lifts.<ref>W.T. Gan, Y. Qiu, and S. Takeda (2014) "The Regularized Siegel–Weil Formula (The Second Term Identity) and the Rallis Inner Product Formula," Inventiones Math. 198, 739–831</ref>
